Desenvolvemos ferramentas para tornar o seu site à prova de falhas e torna-lo numa verdadeira máquina de conversão e vendas.

## Marketing Digital acessível para empresas e negociantes

Esclareça suas dúvidas e comece com uma avaliação gratuita sem riscos.

Posso testar os serviços sem pagar?

Sim. Gostamos de certificar que você se sinta seguro antes de pagar pelos nossos serviços. Apenas diga-nos o que precisa e nós iremos mostrar o que podemos fazer por si sem nenhum custo.

O Marketing Digital é indispensável?

O marketing digital ajuda você a construir seu negócio online e a gerar resultados por meio de diferentes canais e plataformas. Se deseja aumentar o alcance do seu negócio, os Serviços de Marketing Digital são essenciais e altamente recomendáveis, pois você tem a oportunidade de alcançar e interagir intimamente com o seu público-alvo.

Qual serviço é o mais importante?

Se prentende começar absolutamente do zero a sua jornada digital, é essencial que tenha um website profissional para o seu negócio, pois este será a casa oficial da sua marca na internet.

Como é que funciona o vosso serviço de SEO?

A optimização para mecanismos de pesquisa (do inglês Search Engine Optimization), mais comumente conhecida como SEO, é um método para obter mais tráfego para um site por meio de consultas de pesquisa orgânica. A atenção que reserva para o SEO determina como o seu conteúdo é catalogado e, em última análise, como ele se classifica quando as pessoas procuram seus serviços nos motores de pesquisa como o Google.

Quanto custa desenvolver um site?

De sofisticados sites corporativos a grandes e envolventes portais de comércio eletrônico, nós projetamos tudo. Nossos serviços direcionados para web designs resolvem problemas reais de negócios – lindamente. Os nossos de criação de sites partem de 15000MT.

Você gerem contas nas redes sociais?

Absolutamente. Além de cuidar de toda a estratégia de marketing para mídias sociais, também criamos conteúdo para manter o seu público engajado ao mesmo tempo que atrai mais seguidores.

Tenho garantia de resultados?

Claro! A Lugela Digital é uma agência especializada em Marketing de performance, você contrata os nossos serviços para atingir um objectivo e nós entregamos resultados mensuráveis e quantificáveis.

Qual é o budget ideal sucesso garantido?

Infelizmente cada negócio tem necessidades, objectivos e públicos distintos, o que torna extremamente difícil que possamos estimar um custo universal para todos os negócios. No entanto você pode resultados satisfatórios sem gastar muito.

# The state of ICT in Mozambique

By: [Alison Gillwald](https://researchictafrica.net/author/alison-gillwald/ "Alison Gillwald"), [Onkokame Mothobi](https://researchictafrica.net/author/onkokame-mothobi/ "Onkokame Mothobi"), Broc Rademan

*   January 31, 2019

*   [Policy paper](https://researchictafrica.net/research-type/policy-paper/)

*   [After Access](https://researchictafrica.net/tag/after-access/), [After Access Surveys 2018](https://researchictafrica.net/tag/after-access-surveys-2018/), [Global South](https://researchictafrica.net/tag/global-south/), [ICT access and usage survey](https://researchictafrica.net/tag/ict-access-and-usage-survey/), [International Development Research Centre (IDRC)](https://researchictafrica.net/tag/international-development-research-centre-idrc/), [Mozambique](https://researchictafrica.net/tag/mozambique/), [policy paper](https://researchictafrica.net/tag/policy-paper/), [Policy Papers Series 5 | After Access: Assessing Digital Inequality in Africa](https://researchictafrica.net/tag/policy-papers-series-5-after-access-assessing-digital-inequality-in-africa/)

###### Pol**icy Paper Series 5: After Access-Assessing digital inequality in Africa  
Policy Paper No. 6: The state of ICT in Mozambique**

Mozambique has a challenging path ahead if it is to realise the full potential of the ICT sector in developing its economy and to make progress on the information communication technology targets that are intended as enabling the achievement of the United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goals.

**Market structure**

The telecommunications market is structured around four vertically-integrated operators, including fixed-line incumbent, Telecomunicações de Moçambique (TDM). Competition in the mobile market increased following the launch of the third player Movitel, a joint venture between the Viettel Group of Vietnam and Mozambique’s SPI (Management and Investment), a holding company of Mozambique’s ruling Frelimo Party, in 2011. This ended the duopoly of Vodacom Mozambique and mCel, the incumbent mobile subsidiary of the national operator, TDM.

Mozambique’s communication market structure is rare in Africa in that it has inter-platform competition in most of the provincial capitals, with TV Cabo offering an alternative to mobile broadband. TV Cabo offers no voice services, as its telecommunications services are licensed as an Internet service provider. Internet packages offered by TV Cabo are priced higher than mobile operators, but they offer much higher bandwidth and data caps[\[1\]](applewebdata://C020DF0F-B20C-4DC9-8692-2E47F2940365#_ftn1).

Competition in the mobile market increased following the launch of the third player Movitel, a joint venture between the Viettel Group of Vietnam and Mozambique’s SPI (Management and Investment), a holding company of Mozambique’s ruling Frelimo Party, in 2011. This ended the duopoly of Vodacom Mozambique and mCel, the incumbent mobile subsidiary of the national operator, TDM.

**Communication Penetration**

According to the 2017 After Access Survey conducted across 16 countries in Global South, Mozambique had among the lowest mobile phone and Internet penetration rates, 30% and 10%, respectively.

Overall the telecommunications revenue has been declining as a result of the drop in the fixed line revenue. The mobile sector revenue declined from 2014 which may be attributable to pricing pressure from the third entrant, Movitel, in the saturated voice market. Operators in Mozambique have not transitioned to generating significant revenues from data as they have in more mature mobile data markets.

The low-cost service strategy adopted by the third entrant, Movitel, helped it to win a significant revenue share, primarily from mCel, gaining about 11 percent in 2012 and subsequently increasing its revenue share to 27 percent in 2016, leaving mCel with only 21 percent of the total mobile revenue.

Vodacom’s data revenue grew by 31 percent and data customers increased by 63.6 percent, reaching MZN3.7 million, but this is off a very low base and voice revenues remain its dominant source of revenues, unlike in the South Africa market where revenues from data now exceed its voice revenues.

The 1GB data pricing information from the RAMP shows that fierce pricing competition among operators has resulted in low data prices. Among 49 African countries, Research ICT Africa ranks Mozambique third above Ghana, Kenya and South Africa.

**Market Challenges**

**Gender Gap:**Mozambique has the lowest mobile phone adoption level (50%) and the second highest gender disparity at 36 percent after Rwanda’s 38 percent. More than half of all men (50%) have mobile phones as compared to only 32 percent of women.

**Rural-Urban divide:**Rural inhabitants are mostly subsistence farmers and despite Movitel’s rural strategy, the After Access Survey shows that very few households in rural areas have access to telecommunication services.

**Affordability:**Affordability of devices and e-literacy are the main barriers to Internet access in Mozambique. Of those who are offline (90%), 76 percent stated that they do not have devices to access the Internet, while 14 percent stated they do not know how to use the Internet. When asked why they do not have a mobile phone, 78 percent of the respondents stated that they cannot afford a mobile phone. A substantial proportion (36%) of those who do not have mobile phones reported lack of electricity as the main reason why they do not have mobile phones.

**Smartphone penetration:**Mozambique stands at seven percent, which explains the low ten percent, Internet penetration in Mozambique. When respondents where asked why they do not have smartphones, about two-thirds (64%) stated that smartphones are too expensive and 21 percent said that they do not need them, while nine percent reported that they are too complicated to use

**Lack of energy:**Half of the Mozambican population has no access to electricity, compared to only six percent in South Africa and 33 percent in Nigeria. Rural households, which are mostly either not connected to the main electricity grid or have no electricity at all, are less likely to have telecommunication services than urban households.

**Financial inclusion:**Access to formal financial services is extremely limited in Mozambique. The majority of rural area inhabitants do not have access to banking facilities and are normally left out of the formal banking services. Mozambican authorities passed legislation in 2004 allowi
